checks: e_min <= 1.1547*s and e_min > s for every row (hex across-corners limit), e.g. M12 23.91 vs 25.4

shape_hint: A friction-grip structural bolting set: a heavy hexagon-head bolt (large across-flats s, head height k, plain shank ds then a thread of length b) with a heavy hexagon nut (height m, same s) and one round flat washer (hole d1, outside diameter d2, thickness h) placed under the nut or head.

role_map.s: hex width across flats (bolt and nut)

notes: Structural friction-grip HV set per DIN 6914 (bolt) + DIN 6915 (nut) + DIN 6916 (round washer); these are the DIN predecessors of EN 14399-4 (bolt, nut) and EN 14399-6 (chamfered washer) and the dimensions s, e, k, ds, m, d1, d2, h in the EN 14399-4 pages of Fuller/torqbolt are identical for the sizes checked (M12-M36) - but the EN washer has a chamfer and EN bolts list a different b reference (23, 28, 33, 34, 39, 41, 44, 52). KS B 1010 (F10T) and ISO 7412 were NOT verified against text; the F10T set is dimensionally the same family but confirm before printing 'KS'. b1 = thread length b for nominal lengths above the stepped line in the standard (shorter bolts), b2 for the longer ones; the step-line lengths are not tabulated. Nut m is the standard's 'm' (max = nominal). M24 values with 3+ sources (bolt/washer only): P 3, s 41, e_min 45.2, k 15, ds 23.16..24.84, b 34 / 37, washer d1 25, d2 44, h 4; nut height m for M24 is 19 or 20 depending on edition - unresolved, so the M24 row is not published. Typos found: fasten.it nut M24 e_min 45.02 (45.2), boltingspecialist nut M27 e_min 50.35 (50.85). Washer thickness and nut/bolt chamfer features not included.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live all 11 HTML pages (200) and 3 PDFs (read only). 7 rows (M12,16,20,22,27,30,36) x 14 cols x {fasten.it, fasteners.eu, Fuller, Boltport}: 98 cells, only deviation = Boltport 6915 e_min M27 50.35 (typo; Boltport 6914 and 3 others 50.85). Non-PDF clusters per column: P,s,e_min,k,b1,b2,m = 4; ds_min, ds_max, m_min = 3 (fasten.it, fasteners.eu, Fuller); wd1, wd2, wh = 3 (fasten.it, fasteners.eu, Boltport). P also in 4 thread charts. Sanity: e_min<=1.1547 s and >s, ds_min<d<ds_max, k<m, m_min<m, washer d1=d+1, monotone growth.
problems: washer cols wd1/wd2/wh rest on fasten.it + fasteners.eu + Boltport only (PDF excluded, no Fuller DIN 6916). Boltport 6916 table duplicates fasteners.eu's full column structure (c, e columns that fasten.it omits) while carrying its own M36 h-max typo (5.6 vs 6.6) -> if the maintainer treats Boltport as a derivative of fasteners.eu the washer columns fall to 2 clusters and must be dropped.

b1/b2: fasten.it labels the pair 'b min÷max' (different meaning from the 'above/below stepped line' of fasteners.eu / Fuller and 'L<=x / L>=y' of Boltport). Role (short vs long bolts) is header-proven by fasteners.eu, Fuller, Boltport = 3 clusters; fasten.it supports numbers only.
ds_min, ds_max, m_min, wd*, wh sit at exactly 3 clusters (no slack).
row M24 correctly dropped (nut m 19 vs 20, m_min 17.7 vs 18.7: fasten.it itself prints both editions).
one row merges three standards (DIN 6914 bolt, 6915 nut, 6916 washer; DIN 6914/6916 flagged 'Withdrawn' by fasten.it); EN 14399 / KS B 1010 claims in notes are unverified and not backed by cells.
